findings.title: The triage's pause/stop/shutdown kill path is untested — only the alt+x chord is covered
findings.detail: The new drain test covers `/goal pause` and `/goal stop` (`drainCases = ["pause", "stop"]`, line 1248) and the alt+x chord is covered at line 1139, but the third drain named in the test's own comment — `session_shutdown` — is still not exercised for the triage. session_shutdown is the only drain that sets the `shuttingDown` latch (extensions/goal.ts:1896), and that latch is a separate term in the triage's post-abort re-check `if (shuttingDown || stopped || !goal || goal.status !== "active")` (extensions/goal.ts:2123); pause/stop only exercise `stopped`/`goal.status`. The verify path has exactly this test ("session_shutdown during a settle check resolves silently", tests/goal.test.ts:2137), so a regression that drops `shuttingDown` from the triage guard — or lets the triage abort fall through to the aborted-notice branch — would queue a follow-up continuation that outlives a reload/quit (the code comment at goal.ts:2120-2122 says pi honors such a queued continue) with nothing failing in the suite.
findings.recommendation: Add a session_shutdown case to the triage drain test (real-timer triage that never resolves without the signal), asserting the settle resolves `undefined` and `sentCustom` stays empty.

findings.title: Untrusted tool output is copied raw into the judge's prompt, and the judge's verdict then steers the agent in the harness's voice
findings.detail: The previous review's escaping fix covers the triage's *reason* (renderTriagePrompt now JSON.stringify's it, 1288-1294), but the triage's input is still spliced raw: `buildTriageTask` interpolates `ctx.workDigest` verbatim into the child's task at line 976, and the digest is session content — tool results clipped to 240 chars each (817), command arguments (809) — which the agent's tools read from files/network and which the tool-less child (SETTLE_TRIAGE_AGENT, 951-964) is told to treat as data. Content that nevertheless steers the child into emitting a `{"action":"continue"}` object is authoritative for the gate: parseTriageVerdict (927-946) returns the first candidate from jsonCandidates (732-750) with a valid action anywhere in the reply, so an echoed/injected object that appears before the model's own verdict is what the settle handler acts on (`if (triaged?.action === "continue")`, 2172), suppressing the verify for that settle. Impact is bounded — the child is tool-less, the continuation cap still breaks an endless run (2011-2049), and a false `complete` is still blocked by the completion-time verify (`runGatedVerify(goal, goal.verify, "completion")`, 2623-2624) — so this is an injection path that degrades measurement, not a gate bypass.
findings.recommendation: Mark digest-borne text structurally (quote each digest line with an explicit "from tool output" tag) rather than relying on a system-prompt sentence, and keep the steer text framed as quoted evidence rather than the extension's own directive.

findings.title: The judge's task — a 6 KB digest of session content, including tool output — is passed to the child as a command-line argument
findings.detail: createLlmSettleTriage calls `await childRunner(SETTLE_TRIAGE_AGENT, buildTriageTask(goal, ctx), ...)` (990-996); the default runner is `runChild`, which spawns the `pi` binary with the task in argv — `buildChildArgs` ends with `args.push("--", task)` (extensions/subagents.ts:301) and `spawnFn("pi", buildChildArgs(...))` (subagents.ts:461). So the whole triage task, digest included (assistant notes, the commands run, up to 240 chars of each tool result, 770-817), sits in the child's `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` for the duration of the run and is readable with `ps` by any local user on a shared host. The milestone judge already has this shape, but the triage adds a default-on second instance of it for verify goals, on the per-settle path.
findings.recommendation: Pass the task body on stdin (or via a temp file/fd) and keep only flags in argv.

findings.title: PI_GOAL_TRIAGE is documented as opt-in but defaults ON, silently adding an LLM child call per settle for every verify goal
findings.detail: The env's own doc comment here says "Default ON" and PI_GOAL_TRIAGE=0 is the opt-out (line 619-623), and `registerGoalTool` does build the default LLM triage whenever `parseJudgeEnabled(process.env.PI_GOAL_TRIAGE)` is true (line 1723-1735), i.e. when the variable is simply unset (parseJudgeEnabled, 590-593: unset/blank → GOAL_JUDGE_DEFAULT=true). Yet the construction-site comment at 1721-1722 still describes the same switch as "opt-in like the judge — every LLM call at the settle boundary is deliberate configuration". Net effect for a user who never set any PI_GOAL_* variable: every verify goal now gets an extra tool-less child model call (inheriting the session model unless PI_GOAL_JUDGE_MODEL pins one) at each due settle, and that child is fed `ctx.workDigest`, i.e. assistant notes, the commands run, up to 160 chars of arguments and up to 240 chars of each tool result (buildWorkDigest, 770-817). That is a second, default-on egress of session content to a model provider, on a code path the user did not configure; the milestone judge has the same default, but it only applies to verify-less goals, whereas this one touches every verify goal.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the comment at goal.ts:1720 to say the triage is ON by default and PI_GOAL_TRIAGE=0 opts out, matching GOAL_TRIAGE_ENV's comment and the README.

findings.title: The triage-continue path leaves the cached measurement's age frozen, so the prompt's staleness never advances
findings.detail: `lastCheckAge` is documented as "how many continuations ago [the last verify] ran" (goal.ts:1747-1748) and is advanced exactly once per non-due settle (`check = lastCheck!; lastCheckAge += 1;`, goal.ts:2343-2344), which keeps `lastCheckAge === continuations - <continuation the check ran at>`. The new triage-continue branch increments only `continuations` (goal.ts:2158) and returns before that aging, while both consumers read the frozen value: `renderTriagePrompt(..., lastCheck ? lastCheckAge : 0)` (goal.ts:2168) and `staleContinuations: lastCheck ? lastCheckAge : 0` (goal.ts:2177). With PI_GOAL_CHECK_EVERY > 1 — the only configuration where the age can be non-zero — every mid-work triage between two measurements leaves the count one short, and since the prompt's stale clause only renders when the value is > 0, the agent can be told nothing about a measurement that is several continuations old (the row likewise reads "measured N turn(s) ago" with a too-small N). The loop's own design treats staleness as load-bearing (renderCheckPrompt's comment about not presenting a stale timeout as just-happened).
findings.recommendation: In the triage-continue branch, age the cache like a reused measurement (`if (lastCheck) lastCheckAge += 1;`) before rendering the prompt, so the reported age always counts the continuations since the last actual verify.

findings.title: The triage-continue path reports a frozen stale age (lastCheckAge never advances, and its branch is untested)
findings.detail: The triage-continue prompt is built with `lastCheck ? lastCheckAge : 0` (goal.ts:2168) and the row with `staleContinuations: lastCheck ? lastCheckAge : 0` (goal.ts:2177), but `lastCheckAge` is only advanced in the measured-reuse branch (`else { check = lastCheck!; lastCheckAge += 1; }`, goal.ts:2343-2344) and reset to 0 whenever a check runs (goal.ts:2339). The triage-continue branch returns before that, and the triage only runs inside the `if (due)` block (goal.ts:2058-2060), so with the default checkEvery=1 every triage-continue settle leaves the age at 0: renderTriagePrompt's staleness clause (`lastCheckStale > 0`, goal.ts:1298) never fires and the agent is told nothing about how old the last measurement is, no matter how many turns were skipped — unlike the verify path, whose age is reported and tested (tests/goal.test.ts:2899). No test exercises renderTriagePrompt with a non-zero `lastCheckStale`, nor the triage path after a prior measurement, so nothing catches it.
findings.recommendation: Advance the age on a triage-continue settle (e.g. `lastCheckAge += 1` in that branch, or track the continuation index of the last measurement) and add a test that runs one measured settle followed by one triage-continue and asserts the prompt/row carries the aged count.

findings.title: Judge-authored `remaining` text is still the continuation window's measured state — a reworded plateau still reads as progress and resets the cap
findings.detail: Unchanged by this diff and still valid. `recordBudgetOutput(budgetOutputs, judged ? `${lastCheckKind ?? "unavailable"}:[${[...lastJudgeRemaining].sort().join("|")}]` : check.output)` (goal.ts:2354-2357) stores judge prose: `lastJudgeRemaining` comes straight from `verdict.remaining` (goal.ts:2341), free-form short strings the judge re-words each call, and defaultProgressJudge compares only the first and last window entries (goal.ts:564-573). A plateau the judge describes with different wording ("wire the badge" → "wire in-browser badge") therefore reads as "measured state changed" and grants a budget reset up to maxProgressResets. The test that pins this property holds `remaining` fixed and varies only `reason` (tests/goal.test.ts:2470), so the reworded-remaining case is untested, and the comment above the line ("same assessment ⇒ identical string") only holds when the judge repeats its wording verbatim.
findings.recommendation: Record only non-model-authored state for judge checks (the verdict alone, or the judge's item count), or normalize/lowercase+dedupe the remaining set so wording drift cannot register as movement.

findings.title: renderTriagePrompt's escaping of the triage's reason is not pinned by any test
findings.detail: renderTriagePrompt splices the model-authored triage reason through `JSON.stringify` (extensions/goal.ts:1296) — the same escaping the milestone prompt has a dedicated test for ("escapes judge free text so it cannot re-open the prompt's line structure", tests/goal.test.ts:580). The new triage-prompt test passes only a benign reason and asserts `toContain("mid-work on P2")`, and the settle-level test asserts `toContain("porting KVarN P2")` (line 1091) — both still pass if `JSON.stringify` is removed and the reason is concatenated raw, so the boundary this change just fixed has no regression protection. A reason containing `"\n\nGOAL #1 — turn-end triage:"` (the digest fed to the triage includes attacker-influenceable tool output) would again re-open the prompt's own line structure unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add a case to the renderTriagePrompt describe block: pass a reason with quotes/newlines and a criterion containing a newline, then assert the judge line is a single escaped line and that the injected text never appears as a standalone line — the same shape as the milestone escaping test.

findings.title: The default triage factory's tool-less agent and session-model inheritance are unpinned
findings.detail: `createLlmSettleTriage` is only reached through registerGoalTool with `triageRunChildFn`, and the two tests that exercise it pass `judgeModel: "fast/small"` (line 1226) or no model at all (the settle ctx has no `model`, line 1298). So neither the tool-less agent def nor the `sessionModel: () => sessionModelRef` wiring (extensions/goal.ts:1731) is covered: giving the triage child tools, or dropping the sessionModel getter, breaks nothing in the suite. The milestone judge — the same machinery — has both tests (`expect(seen[0]!.agent).toMatchObject({ tools: [] })` at line 629 and "the default judge construction inherits the session model" at line 2499), and the README advertises the triage as tool-less and inheriting the session model unless PI_GOAL_JUDGE_MODEL pins one.
findings.recommendation: Add a `createLlmSettleTriage` unit test mirroring `createLlmSettleJudge`: assert the agent handed to the runner has `tools: []`, that the session model resolved from a sessionModel getter reaches the runner, and that a pinned model wins — or extend the registration test at line 1206 with a `ctx.model` and a task assertion.

findings.title: Cap test claims judge reasons are read as the measured state, but its window holds one output so the property is never exercised
findings.detail: Still valid. With `maxContinuations: 1` (tests/goal.test.ts:2447) the window holds exactly one entry when the cap judge runs, so the test only pins defaultProgressJudge's "fewer than two measured states → fail closed" branch (goal.ts:566-567). Its name and inline comment assert a mapping the code does not have: the window stores `verdict:[sorted remaining]` (goal.ts:2354-2356), never the judge's reason. The plateau direction for judge-derived strings is now pinned by the neighbouring test (`expect(windows).toEqual([["working:[badge]", "working:[badge]"]])`, tests/goal.test.ts:2495), but the granted-reset direction for judge-derived window strings is still only exercised with verify outputs (tests/goal.test.ts:2707).
findings.recommendation: Retitle the test to what it verifies (a one-entry window fails closed), or raise maxContinuations ≥ 2 with a progressJudge spy that asserts the recorded strings and a changed judge state granting a reset.
